claim: Conductances of ion channels and transporters controlling cardiac excitation may vary in a population of subjects with different cardiac gene expression patterns.
source: Conductances of ion channels and transporters controlling cardiac excitation may vary in a population of subjects with different cardiac gene expression patterns.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a premise for the study.

claim: The amount of variability in conductances and its origin are not quantitatively known.
source: However, the amount of variability and its origin are not quantitatively known.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a knowledge gap.

claim: Combinations of conductances can generate a normal intracellular Ca2+ transient without any constraint on the action potential.
source: We propose a new conceptual approach to predict this variability that consists of finding combinations of conductances generating a normal intracellular Ca2+ transient without any constraint on the action potential.
evidence: This is the central methodological approach described in the abstract.

claim: The Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel is a model system of genetically diverse mouse strains that allows quantification of inter-subject versus intra-subject variability.
source: Furthermore, we validate experimentally its predictions using the Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel, a model system of genetically diverse mouse strains that allows us to quantify inter-subject versus intra-subject variability.
evidence: This describes the experimental validation approach using the HMDP.

claim: Conductances of inward Ca2+ and outward K+ currents compensate each other to generate a normal Ca2+ transient.
source: The method predicts that conductances of inward Ca2+ and outward K+ currents compensate each other to generate a normal Ca2+ transient in good quantitative agreement with current measurements in ventricular myocytes from hearts of different isogenic strains.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: A feedback mechanism sensing the aggregate Ca2+ transient of the heart suffices to regulate ionic conductances.
source: Our results suggest that a feedback mechanism sensing the aggregate Ca2+ transient of the heart suffices to regulate ionic conductances.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract.

claim: Electrophysiological models of increasing complexity have been developed to describe the cardiac action potential and its interaction with the intracellular calcium signal.
source: Following the landmark publication of the Hodgkin-Huxley model of nerve-cell action potential over six decades ago (Hodgkin and Huxley, 1952), electrophysiological models of increasing complexity have been developed to describe the cardiac action potential (AP) and its interaction with the intracellular calcium (Ca2+) signal (Noble, 2011; Silva and Rudy, 2010), which links electrical signaling to mechanical contraction in cardiomycoytes (Bers, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The intracellular calcium signal links electrical signaling to mechanical contraction in cardiomyocytes.
source: Following the landmark publication of the Hodgkin-Huxley model of nerve-cell action potential over six decades ago (Hodgkin and Huxley, 1952), electrophysiological models of increasing complexity have been developed to describe the cardiac action potential (AP) and its interaction with the intracellular calcium (Ca2+) signal (Noble, 2011; Silva and Rudy, 2010), which links electrical signaling to mechanical contraction in cardiomycoytes (Bers, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bers, 2001.

claim: Population-averaged models fall short of predicting how different individuals in a genetically diverse population respond to perturbations.
source: While such prototypical 'population-averaged' (and even 'species-averaged') models have proven useful to investigate basic mechanisms of cardiac arrhythmias on cellular to tissue scales (Krogh-Madsen and Christini, 2012; Karma, 2013; Qu et al., 2014), they fall short of predicting how different individuals in a genetically diverse population respond to perturbations (such as physiological stressors, ion channel mutations, drug or gene therapies, etc.) affecting one or several cellular components.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of traditional models with citations.

claim: Ion channel conductances can exhibit a high degree of activity-dependent plasticity as well as variability between individuals.
source: In a neuroscience context, the limitation of population-averaged models has been highlighted by pioneering theoretical and experimental studies by Abbot, Marder, and co-workers demonstrating that ion channel conductances can exhibit a high degree of activity-dependent plasticity as well as variability between individuals (LeMasson et al., 1993; Siegel et al., 1994; Liu et al., 1998; Golowasch et al., 1999; Prinz et al., 2004; Schulz et al., 2006; Marder and Goaillard, 2006; Grashow et al., 2009; Marder, 2011; O'Leary et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to neuroscience studies.

claim: Intracellular Ca2+ concentration is used as an activity-dependent feedback mechanism regulating ion channel conductance values.
source: This question was addressed by treating ion channel conductances as dynamical variables in models of neuronal activity and by using the intracellular Ca2+ concentration as an activity-dependent feedback mechanism regulating their values (LeMasson et al., 1993; Siegel et al., 1994; Liu et al., 1998), a mechanism supported by experiments (Golowasch et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to theoretical and experimental studies.

claim: A similar bursting activity could be obtained with multiple parameter sets in computational models of the crustacean somato-gastric ganglion.
source: Subsequently, a different type of computational study in which model parameters (conductances and synaptic strengths of a circuit model of the crustacean somato-gastric ganglion) were varied randomly, demonstrated that a similar bursting activity could be obtained with multiple parameter sets, that is multiple 'good enough solutions' (GES) (Prinz et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Prinz et al., 2004.

claim: Neurons of the same circuits obtained from different crabs could have markedly different ion channel densities but yet different circuits could generate similar bursting activities.
source: This prediction agreed qualitatively with an experimental study demonstrating that neurons of the same circuits obtained from different crabs could have markedly different ion channel densities, corresponding to different gene expression, but yet different circuits could generate similar bursting activities (Schulz et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schulz et al., 2006.

claim: Different circuits, while operating similarly under controlled conditions, could respond differently to perturbations such as serotonin addition.
source: A later experimental study further showed that different circuits, while operating similarly under controlled conditions, could respond differently to perturbations such as serotonin addition, which increases the bursting frequency at a population level, but lowers it in some individuals (Grashow et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Grashow et al., 2009.

claim: The existence of different good enough solutions provides an evolutionary advantage for the survival of a genetically diverse population.
source: In addition, they suggest that the existence of different good enough solutions provides an evolutionary advantage for the survival of a genetically diverse population by allowing different individuals to better adapt to different environmental challenges so as to survive and restore the population.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited studies.

claim: Increasing SERCA magnitude increases SR Ca2+ load, thereby increasing the amount of SR Ca2+ release and CaT amplitude, but at the same time depletes Ca2+ from the cytosol.
source: Increasing SERCA magnitude increases SR Ca2+ load, thereby increasing the amount of SR Ca2+ release and CaT amplitude, but at the same time depletes Ca2+ from the cytosol.
evidence: This is an inference based on the model behavior.

claim: Inter-strain variability of ion channel conductances can be distinguished from cell-to-cell variability of those same quantities for a significant number of the strains investigated.
source: We conclude that inter-strain variability of ion channel conductances can be distinguished from cell-to-cell variability of those same quantities for a significant number of the strains investigated.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Mean values of cell shortening do not vary substantially across strains.
source: The results in Figure 4B, which use contraction as a surrogate for CaT amplitude, support this hypothesis by showing that mean values of cell shortening do not vary substantially across strains.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Cell shortening measurements for the six strains reported do not originate from different distributions within statistical uncertainty.
source: This is confirmed by performing a standard ANOVA statistical test, which shows that cell shortening measurements for the six strains reported in Figure 4B do not originate from different distributions within statistical uncertainty (p-value p=0.4136).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Compensation remains operative at the organ scale because CaT amplitude histograms have similar means with and without electrical coupling.
source: In summary, our results show that compensation remains operative at the organ scale because CaT amplitude histograms have similar means with and without electrical coupling (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by computational simulations shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Gap junctional coupling has the additional important effect of reducing CaT amplitude variability, thereby promoting tight organ-level behavior despite high cell-to-cell variability.
source: Gap junctional coupling has the additional important effect of reducing CaT amplitude variability, thereby promoting tight organ-level behavior despite high cell-to-cell variability.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on computational simulations.

claim: Intracellular Ca2+ overload activating the Ca2+-calcineurin-NFAT signaling pathway has been shown to play a major role in cardiac hypertrophy.
source: Although many factors contribute to the hypertrophic response in the HMDP (Rau et al., 2017; Santolini et al., 2018), intracellular Ca2+ overload activating the Ca2+-calcineurin-NFAT signaling pathway has been shown to play a major role (Bers, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bers, 2008.

claim: Ca2+ sensing suffices to produce a physiological AP waveform whose duration spans comparable range to that recorded experimentally in isolated myocytes, even though the voltage signal is not used to constrain model parameters.
source: A remarkable and nontrivial finding of the present computational study is that Ca2+ sensing suffices to produce a physiological AP waveform whose duration spans comparable range (see Figure 5C) to that recorded experimentally in isolated myocytes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), even though the voltage signal is not used to constrain model parameters.
evidence: This is supported by computational results shown in Figure 5C and experimental data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Different GES exhibit similar CaT amplitude versus pacing frequency curves consistent with experimental measurements over a broad range of pacing frequencies from 0.5 to 4 Hz.
source: Even though the GES search was performed using target values of Ca2+ sensors for a 4 Hz pacing frequency, different GES exhibit similar CaT amplitude versus pacing frequency curves consistent with experimental measurements (Figure 18 in Bondarenko et al., 2004) over a broad range of pacing frequencies from 0.5 to 4 Hz.
evidence: This is supported by computational results and citation to Bondarenko et al., 2004.

claim: The HMDP consists of a population of over 100 inbred mouse strains selected for usage in systematic genetic analyses of complex traits.
source: The hybrid mouse diversity panel (HMDP) consists of a population of over 100 inbred mouse strains selected for usage in systematic genetic analyses of complex traits (Ghazalpour et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ghazalpour et al., 2012.

claim: The main goals in selecting the HMDP strains were to increase resolution of genetic mapping, have a renewable resource available to all investigators world-wide, and provide a shared data repository.
source: The main goals in selecting the strains were to (i) increaseresolution of genetic mapping, (ii) have a renewable resource that is available to all investigators world-wide, and (iii) provide a shared data repository (https://systems.genetics.ucla.edu/about/hmdp2) that would allow the integration of data across multiple scales, including genomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic, proteomic, and clinical phenotypes.
evidence: This describes the design goals of the HMDP.

claim: The cell isolation procedure typically yielded 30-50% of rod-shaped and Ca2+-tolerant myocytes.
source: This procedure typically yielded 30 – 50% of rod-shaped and Ca2+-tolerant myocytes.
evidence: This describes the experimental method and its typical yield.

claim: The mathematical model of mouse ventricular myocytes combines elements of previously published ventricular myocyte models.
source: We have developed a novel mathematical model of mouse ventricular myocytes that combines elements of previously published ventricular mycoyte models (Shiferaw et al., 2003; Shannon et al., 2004; Bondarenko et al., 2004; Mahajan et al., 2008).
evidence: This describes the computational model development.

claim: The Bondarenko et al., 2004 mouse model has sarcolemmal currents fitted to detailed experimental measurements of sarcolemmal currents in mouse ventricular myocytes.
source: The Bondarenko et al., 2004 mouse model has sarcolemmal currents fitted to detailed experimental measurements of sarcolemmal currents in mouse ventricular myocytes.
evidence: This describes a feature of the Bondarenko model with citation.

claim: The Shiferaw et al. model represents the release of calcium from the SR as a sum of individual spark events, which reproduces important observed instabilities such as Ca2+ transient alternans.
source: The Shiferaw et al. (2003) model represents the release of calcium from the SR as a sum of individual spark events, which reproduces important observed instabilities such as Ca2+ transient alternans.
evidence: This describes a feature of the Shiferaw model with citation.

claim: The combined model reproduces well the mouse electrophysiological phenotype of the Bondarenko et al., 2004 model while being computationally efficient and incorporating a realistic description of Ca2+ cycling.
source: However, we checked that our combined model reproduces well the mouse electrophysiological phenotype of the Bondarenko et al., 2004 model while being computationally efficient and incorporating a realistic description of Ca2+ cycling.
evidence: This describes a validation of the computational model.

claim: The force-frequency relationship produced by the model has the correct negative staircase observed experimentally.
source: We also verified that the force-frequency relationship produced by the model has the correct negative staircase observed experimentally.
evidence: This describes a validation of the computational model.

claim: The codes used in this work are available at: https://github.com/circs/GES.
source: The codes used in this work are available at: https://github.com/circs/GES (Rees, 2018; copy archived at https://github.com/elifesciences-publications/GES).
evidence: This provides information about code availability.
